texts: good. the walk, Bevin and the Cove Stair are all present, with late summer, Year 1 and sundown kept as separate time atoms and 'one day before the autumn equinox' carried as a measured one-day gap to the equinox.

good. the explicit 'of the Stilllight Lantern' licenses the part link from the iron bands to the lantern, and the touching parses as an ordinary past event; note the bands are touched as one group, not band by band.
good. a plain past lighting event with Bevin as the agent and the lantern as the thing changed.

mixed: the burning, its dusk-to-dawn interval and its tense are all recorded, but the bare mass object 'mire-essence' lands as the kind symbol rather than a specific quantity, so what burns here never connects to 'the mire-essence of the Stilllight Lantern' that is refreshed in sentence 7 - the two share no symbol. Make the fuel the lantern's own so the later mention can refer back to it: 'The Stilllight Lantern burned its mire-essence from dusk until dawn.'
good. a second walk event reusing the same Bevin and Cove Stair symbols, with midnight as its time and the repetition recorded by an 'again' tag.
good. same shape as the midnight walk; 'the third watch' is kept as a bare named-time symbol, which loses nothing even though there is no structured calendar term for a watch.

good. the refreshing, its agent, its midnight time and the lantern's mire-essence are all there; if sentence 4 is rewritten as suggested, this definite will also link back to the essence that burned overnight.
good. the 'of the Stilllight Lantern' genitive licenses the wick-lantern part link, and the trimming parses as a past event at the third watch.
